definition: Polysemanticity is a phenomenon in neural networks in which individual neurons respond to multiple unrelated concepts rather than to a single well-defined one.
details: A polysemantic neuron might activate for legal text, DNA sequences, and Hebrew script simultaneously. Because such neurons cannot be straightforwardly interpreted, polysemanticity is a central obstacle in mechanistic interpretability.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It figures out meaning by noticing which words like to travel together. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Polysemanticity — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
